items.title: Norris takes pole as the official grid matches FIA Document 59
items.summary: The Formula1.com Starting Grid page checked at 18:40 UTC matches FIA Document 59: Stroll 16th, Bottas 17th, Lindblad 18th and Bortoleto 19th after their respective penalties; Norris starts first, Antonelli second and Lawson third. Norris took pole in 1:27.470, 0.204s ahead of Russell. A collector snapshot at 18:36 UTC briefly reverted Lindblad to 12th. The separate Race results page still showed no classification at 18:40 UTC, so no Race result is inferred.
items.why_it_matters: The hash-reviewed FIA final grid remains the durable source across transient collector/cache regressions; starting positions remain separate from qualifying results.

items.title: Four drivers reprimanded over the reconnaissance-lap pit-exit instruction
items.summary: FIA Documents 60–63 record driving reprimands for Nico Hülkenberg (third), Sergio Perez (fourth), Isack Hadjar (second) and Valtteri Bottas (first). Each driver failed to cross the pit-exit white line at the earliest opportunity on reconnaissance laps after not performing a practice start, contrary to Article 12.2.1.i and Race Director Event Note item 5.7. These are reprimands, not grid penalties.
items.why_it_matters: The four decisions clarify the pit-exit instruction immediately before the Race and do not change the final starting order.

sources.label: FIA Race Director’s Competition Notes, Document 34, item 5.7

items.title: Hamilton reaches 400 Formula 1 starts at São Paulo
items.summary: Formula1.com reports that the São Paulo Grand Prix is Lewis Hamilton's 400th Formula 1 race start, after 20 continuous seasons in the championship. Fernando Alonso's São Paulo start is number 445. This is a career milestone, not a claim about the unfinished race result.
items.why_it_matters: It puts Hamilton's longevity in context without conflating a milestone with his current race position or result.

items.title: Drivers warn against repeating Saturday's conditions in the Race
items.summary: George Russell warned that repeating Saturday's opening wet conditions in the Race could create a high risk of a serious incident; Carlos Sainz described the first laps as sketchy, and Isack Hadjar said the full wets lacked grip. These are drivers' assessments after Qualifying, not a Race Control decision or a current forecast. Pirelli's 7 November report cited a 60% race-day rain chance when it was published.
items.why_it_matters: Cars must follow more closely in a race than in qualifying, changing the visibility and aquaplaning risks. Keep Pirelli's dated rain probability separate from the live forecast and any decision to run.

items.title: Pirelli's dry-race projection favors a two-stop strategy
items.summary: Using Friday FP2 as its only representative long-run data, Pirelli estimates a Soft–Medium–Soft two-stop about three seconds quicker than using all three slick compounds, while a one-stop is around ten seconds slower. Coffee Corner Motorsport's Pirelli-credited chart lists additional dry-race scenarios; its complete 22-driver RACE SETS graphic shows the remaining race inventory, not all tyres used during practice. These are pre-race projections, not a live forecast or race outcome.
items.why_it_matters: Wet conditions can displace dry-race simulations. Keep Pirelli's estimates separate from the secondary chart's lap windows and from the actual remaining-set inventory.
